report.question: Which recorded green results are time-decayed - i.e. would return a different verdict today because they query a live advisory or registry database rather than a frozen input?
report.headline: The naive expectation is INVERTED. Over this corpus and this window, the LIVE-QUERY advisory gate did NOT decay - osv-scanner returns the same clean-zero today on two independent signals, even though 5 advisories touching its dependency set moved in the window. What decayed was (a) a stored human RATIONALE about the live database, now contradicted by it, and (b) the DETERMINISTIC-INPUT gates, because 'deterministic-input' means deterministic GIVEN its input, and the input is a source tree that concurrent agents are mutating. A volatility model that classifies gates by which database they query, and stops there, mis-ranks the actual decay risk in this program.

volatility_taxonomy._note: The unit's inputs field offers a two-way split (deterministic-input vs live-query). Measurement forced a THIRD class, and the third class is where the real risk sits.
volatility_taxonomy.LIVE-QUERY: Answer is computed against an external database at run time (osv.dev, the GitHub Actions API). Decays without any local change. Re-runnable, therefore cheap to re-verify.
volatility_taxonomy.MIRROR-OF-LIVE: Answer is computed from local bytes that are a CACHED SNAPSHOT of a live upstream (the claude-plugins-official git mirror). Re-running the probe looks deterministic and returns a stable answer, yet the answer can be wrong about the live world. This is the dangerous class: it FAILS the naive volatility test by looking frozen.
volatility_taxonomy.DETERMINISTIC-INPUT: Answer depends only on bytes in this repo. Immune to database decay - but NOT immune to decay, because the repo is being written concurrently. Deterministic given its input is not the same as frozen.

report.answer_to_the_question: Directly decayed today: T2 (a stored rationale about the live advisory DB, now contradicted by it) and T3 (the CI green, red within the same day at the pinned sha). Partially decayed: T5, where the license verdict holds but 44 of its pinned hash anchors are stale. NOT decayed: T1, the actual live-advisory gate, despite 5 advisories touching its dependency set moving inside the window - because none matched the pinned versions. The finding that matters for the program is that classifying a gate by WHICH DATABASE IT QUERIES predicted the wrong answers here: the live-query scan held, and the greens that broke were a piece of prose and two deterministic-input gates whose input is a concurrently-mutated tree.
report.probe_1_as_specified: 'classify each stored green by input volatility and re-execute every live-query gate today, recording the new verdict alongside the stored one' - DONE. Classification in volatility_taxonomy and gate_inventory[].volatility_class; re-execution recorded per row in gate_inventory[].reprobe_today for T1, T3, T4, T5. T2 was re-executed against the advisory record itself.
report.probe_2_as_specified: 'for gates that cannot be re-run, prove decay indirectly by diffing the upstream advisory feed between the stored timestamp and today and showing whether any advisory touching the dependency set was published in that window' - DONE via the OSV REST querybatch feed diff: 99-package dependency set, 110 advisories touching it, 5 modified inside the 2026-08-09 -> 2026-08-11 window, 3 of them newly published 2026-08-07. Mechanically independent of probe 1: raw HTTP JSON with our own date arithmetic versus a compiled Go binary doing lockfile extraction and version-range matching.
report.method_limitations_inline: The corpus scan covers command-center/** only (665 files); a green recorded elsewhere in the repo and cited informally would be missed - UNVERIFIED, settled by re-running the same discriminator over the whole tree. The CI attribution reads job CONCLUSIONS, not logs, so it establishes WHICH gate failed but not WHY - UNVERIFIED, settled by gh run view --log-failed. The license mirror was not fetched, so 'the mirror moved' is established from its local HEAD date only.
